policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Finish all memory updates from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Dispatch exclusively on the resulting buttons_completed value: if 0, choose A, press the first button; if 1, choose B, press the second button; if 2, neither A nor B is eligible and use the container-handling rules below. Never select a button using the incoming count after updating it, or because a completed button has sprung back. At the initial decision the initialized count is 0, so choose A. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations and prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target. Retry only a button press or pickup not established as completed. This fallback must never override observed completion, restore a removed target, or permit A or B when the updated buttons_completed is 2. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

fields.name: pending_target_positions
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. At every decision, including one whose next command is another button press, process all observed frames chronologically before writing memory or selecting a command. Associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through all observed motion, including residual motion during later pickup or put-down intervals. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. For each rotating pair, estimate its shared center and follow both members' angular progression around that center across intermediate frames. Resolve the two identities jointly, continuing the observed rotation direction rather than independently choosing nearest endpoints. Returning to the same unordered pair of positions does not establish that identities returned: a half-turn exchanges them, and each successive observed exchange must be applied. Update every remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene, including stationary targets whose cube centers must be replaced by their covering containers' centers. If the interval shows the first pending container being grasped and lifted successfully, remove that entry once; a held-container observation continuing into a put-down interval is not a new pickup. Recognize success from the grasp-and-lift transition, supported by the revealed requested cube. Keep tracking the remaining targets during the hand's movements, ignoring small occlusion-induced center wobble. Write [] when none remain. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]

fields.name: buttons_completed
fields.description: Initialize to 0 with empty incoming memory. Start from the incoming count and inspect the entire observed interval for completion of the next required button press. A hand descent to that button followed by withdrawal, with button depression or contact-height evidence, increments the count once, capped at 2. Write this updated count before selecting a command. In particular, incoming 1 plus a completed second press yields 2 even if the button has sprung back in the decision scene. The first menu button is the larger-x button in these scenes; the second is the smaller-x button. A pressed-down label is sufficient supporting evidence but is not mandatory: low contact followed by withdrawal also establishes the press. Preserve the count when buttons spring back and throughout container manipulation. Do not increment merely because a button is visible. e.g. 1
